Find the mode of the following data :
Class0-2020-4040-6060-8080-100100-120120-140
Frequency681012653
items.answer: The maximum frequency 12 belongs to the class 60−80, so 60−80 is the modal class, with l = 60, f₁ = 12, f₀ = 10, f₂ = 6 and h = 20. Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀) ÷ (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h = 60 + [(12 − 10) ÷ (24 − 10 − 6)] × 20 = 60 + (2 × 20) ÷ 8 = 60 + 5 = 65. Hence the mode is 65.

items.answer: Written as a discrete frequency distribution the listed values occur as 13 once, 15 three times, 17 once, 18 three times, 20 three times and 25 three times, with λ still to be placed. items.stem: The mean and median of 100 observation are 50 and 52 respectively. The value of the largest observation is 100. It was later found that it is 110. Find the true mean and median.
items.answer: From Mean = Σfx ÷ Σf we get 50 = Σfx ÷ 100, so Σfx = 5000. Replacing the wrong value 100 by the correct 110 gives the corrected total Σfx′ = 5000 − 100 + 110 = 5010. Correct mean = 5010 ÷ 100 = 50.1. The change affects only the largest observation, which stays largest, so the ordering of the data is unchanged and the median stays as it was. Hence the true mean is 50.1 and the true median is 52.

items.stem: Write the relationship connecting three measures of central tendencies. Hence find the median of the give data if mode is 24.5 and mean is 29.75.
items.answer: The empirical relationship connecting the three measures is 3 × Median = Mode + 2 × Mean. Substituting Mode = 24.5 and Mean = 29.75 gives 3Mᵈ = 24.5 + 2 × 29.75 = 24.5 + 59.50 = 84.0, so Mᵈ = 84 ÷ 3 = 28. Hence the median is 28.
